findings.complete_paragraph: Bratton asks what interfaces, "against a constrained action-space, instead cultivate the abstraction and tolerance for ambiguity that agent orchestration demands" (PDF p. 57). He also asks for design primitives for agent-to-agent interfaces that "presume both cooperation and adversariality as norms" (PDF p. 57). Selection, deferral and revision make the claimed tolerance for ambiguity consequential in the action-space. Cooperation and adversariality require their respective available acts and constraints. Capability also depends upon the [acting harness](../sources/media-technology-philosophy/bratton/bratton-2026-agentworld-brief/SOURCE.md#bratton-2026-agentworld-brief-q038) through which those acts become possible: "capability in deployment is not a property of weights alone. It is a property of the harness — the scaffolding of tools, memory, shared knowledge bases, agent protocols, and institutional interfaces through which a model acts on the world." The claimed distinction must be located in the actual acting ensemble: model, tool, memory, permission, interface or a consequential relation among its participants. The research questions propose design work. They do not report the results of the comparisons required here.

findings.stronger_inference_if_removed: A source question or quoted harness architecture could otherwise establish an executed interface experiment or universal success; removing the scope would silently upgrade locator/readiness.
findings.positive_operation_retained: Selection/deferral/revision and cooperation/adversariality have actual acting loci in the ensemble, with existing quotations retained.

findings.complete_paragraph: **The negative result counts.** A proposed technical relation has to identify an operation and a comparison capable of exercising its difference. A [removal comparison](#3) puts this requirement under pressure: delete the disclosure, sever the challenge route, freeze the evaluator, merge the worlds, close the audit — and inspect the operation in a case that engages the removed route. An unchanged result in a case where the route was never used does not decide the claim. This protects against decoration in both directions: against philosophy that never touches the machine, and against machine features that borrow philosophy's prestige without its operation. The conceptual inquiry receives the test result: a failed test is one of three findings — the implementation is wrong, the operational mapping is inadequate, or the test cannot discriminate the distinction — and each returns the question to a different home. Through [epistemic cultivation](../concepts/C46-Epistemic-Cultivation.md), the finding’s scope, conditions and path of change remain available in the next inquiry. A distinction that passed at one scope can then be tested at another, with its earlier result retained rather than silently made universal.

findings.why_necessary: Removal comparison must engage the removed route and account for competing causes; implementation/mapping/test failure differ.
findings.stronger_inference_if_removed: Null result in an unexercised case could otherwise disprove an operative distinction, or every failure could be blamed on implementation/mapping without identifying cause.
findings.positive_operation_retained: Compare actual disclosed/challenged/permission/evaluator route, retain its scope and revisit at next inquiry.
